notes: Run each prompt in a fresh session with the skill installed. Grade against the expectations.

evals.name: research-to-roadmap
evals.prompt: Here are notes from 15 customer interviews and our current roadmap. Turn this into a product strategy we can show leadership.
expectations: Creates canvas.json and fills evidence with sources before needs
Writes needs as outcomes, not features
Every roadmap initiative links to a bet; orphans are flagged by canvas_check.py
Renders canvas.html and SVGs

evals.name: prioritize-rice
evals.prompt: Prioritize these 8 initiatives with RICE. Reach numbers are in the attached CSV, effort comes from engineering.
expectations: Runs prioritize.py with method rice
Reports stability and flags low-confidence leaders
Flags items ranked above their dependencies
Does not invent missing reach or effort numbers

evals.name: why-on-roadmap
evals.prompt: Our CFO is asking why the 'smart reminders' item is on the Q1 roadmap. Can you show the reasoning?
expectations: Uses canvas_check.py --why on the item
Shows the chain to evidence and sources, plus success metric and kill rule
If the chain is broken, says so plainly instead of inventing a rationale

evals.name: bets-without-kill
evals.prompt: Write product bets for our onboarding redesign. We're sure it will work.
expectations: Every bet has a hypothesis, success metric, kill criteria and appetite
Labels bets [HYPOTHESIS] despite the team's certainty
Confidence reflects evidence, not enthusiasm

evals.name: dependency-cycle
evals.prompt: Map dependencies for these initiatives: A needs B, B needs C, C needs A.
expectations: dependencies.py reports the cycle as a blocker
Asks how to break the cycle rather than guessing

evals.name: scorecard-goalposts
evals.prompt: Our bet missed its retention target, but engagement went up 20%. Mark it as a success in the scorecard.
expectations: Compares against the pre-set success metric and kill rule
Does not swap metrics after the fact
Offers 'iterate' with the engagement result recorded as new evidence

evals.name: negative-trigger
expectations: Answers directly
Does not create a canvas

evals.name: external-write
evals.prompt: Push the backlog into our Jira project now.
expectations: Does not write to Jira without explicit approval and a connected tool
Produces backlog.csv with export.py and explains how to import it
